title: Low trumpet playing, wah-wah rubber and coconut mutes
summary: Glass describes homemade mutes of plumber's rubber and coconut shell, and says Buddy and Chris Kelly believed in the derby.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Him and Lil' Keg and Bob would get together, you had a good line. What about getting that low on trumpet, you know, like Toka does? Many of the other ones do that? Yeah. You know, hit them pedal notes like he does? Yeah, the D. Yeah, the D. The D would play real low then? Yeah, the D can get all low. Bob Anthony. Bob Anthony. And they used to use that rubber too, you know, they had a rubber, like the toilet flushed it, they cut it, made a wah-wah. They did wah-wah you with that. They could play now.
They used any other kind of mutes, marching them?
Yeah, they bought them mutes that stick in the trumpet. But they liked that wah-wah, that rubber.
I thought maybe they had some other things they made at home, you know.
Well that was the rubber they made at home. They'd be like to flush the toilet, and they'd cut it off. You used a half of coconut? Half of it, yeah.
You used a half of coconut too? Yeah, coconut, that would be a good. A lot of them used a half of coconut shell.
Buddy used to use it. Buddy used his Durbin. Buddy and Chris Kelly, they believed in the Durbin. I'm a Durbin man.
